title: Cross-SDK retry/backoff ergonomics, idempotency semantics, and retryable-error taxonomy (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Each SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) has grown ad-hoc retry behaviors and idempotency ergonomics. Customers are confused by inconsistent defaults, differ in when to provide idempotency keys, and see divergent backoff behavior across languages. This leads to operational surprises (duplicate side effects, higher latencies from aggressive retries, or insufficient retries on transient infra errors).
goals: Define one canonical cross-SDK retry/backoff policy surfaced as the default with per-language ergonomic wrappers.
Standardize idempotency key semantics: when SDK auto-generates, how keys are propagated in multipart/streaming requests, and clear guidance for stateful vs stateless endpoints.
Publish a retryable-error taxonomy that SDKs use to classify errors deterministically (retryable, non-retryable, idempotent-only).
Provide code examples for Python/TS/Go showing correct patterns for sync + streaming calls and how to opt out or customize behavior.
non_goals: Changing server-side error codes or adding new API surface beyond headers (we will rely on existing status codes and existing 'Idempotency-Key' header convention).
Implementing automatic external duplicate suppression on the server — server-side dedupe is a follow-up project.
proposal_summary: Default policy (named 'balanced'): initial_delay=150ms, max_delay=5s, multiplier=2.0, max_attempts=5, jitter=full

On idempotent-only endpoints (marked in our OpenAPI catalog) SDK will perform up to max_attempts with exponential backoff; on non-idempotent endpoints SDK default will be fewer attempts (max_attempts=3) and will require explicit idempotency key opt-in to do retries that may cause side effects.

Idempotency key rules: if caller supplies 'Idempotency-Key' header it is used verbatim; otherwise SDK generates a stable per-request UUID unless caller passes "do_not_generate_idempotency_key" option. Generated keys are returned to caller in response metadata when available.

Streaming semantics: for incremental/streaming responses we treat retries as a new logical request; SDK will surface partial data and an explicit 'stream_resume_token' header when server supports resumable streams. By default streaming calls do not auto-retry body-side failures unless idempotency key is present and server advertises resumability.

Retryable-error taxonomy: classify errors into RETRYABLE_TRANSIENT (5xx, network timeouts, connection resets), RETRYABLE_RATE_LIMIT (429 with Retry-After), NON_RETRYABLE_CLIENT (4xx not 429), and IDEMPOTENT_ONLY (application-level 409 with conflict semantics). SDKs will use explicit classifiers with override hooks.
language_specific_notes: Python: expose RetryConfig dataclass and helper decorators (e.g., @redwood.retryable) with context-manager for temporary overrides. Default of 5 attempts for idempotent endpoints; use requests/urllib3 integration for connection-level detection.

TypeScript: provide a fluent builder API (RedwoodRetry.policy().withBackoff(...)) and an option bag for fetch/websocket clients. Browser SDK should favor conservative defaults (max_attempts=3) because of battery/latency concerns.

Go: idiomatic context.Context integration, allow per-request retry via WithRetry(ctx, cfg). Use typed errors and sentinel error values so caller code can switch on errors without string matching. Keep API small and explicit.
examples: Python snippet: client.call.generate(prompt, retry_config=RetryConfig.default()), explains how to pass idempotency_key='abc-123' or leave blank to auto-generate.
TS snippet: const res = await client.chat.create({ messages }, { retry: RedwoodRetry.balanced() }); shows builder usage and opt-out via { retry: null }.
Go snippet: resp, err := client.Create(ctx, req, WithRetry(DefaultBalanced)); demonstrates ctx-based overrides and error type assertions for retryable checks.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc accepted by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and product PM with sign-off recorded in PRD.
Reference implementation merged in all three SDKs with feature flag opt-in behavior for 2 weeks, then flip default after telemetry review.
Unit + integration tests covering classification of at least 12 common error forms (network timeout, connection reset, 429 with/without Retry-After, 5xx, 404/400, 409 conflict).
Examples and migration guide published in the SDK docs; short cookbooks for "making non-idempotent calls safe" and "stream resume best practices".
Telemetry: events emitted for retry attempts, idempotency-key generation, and stream resumptions. Dashboard card added to Console runtime-ops for SLO impact.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Auto-generating idempotency keys could mask duplicate user intent for non-idempotent endpoints. Mitigation: default generation only for endpoints marked idempotent or when caller opts in via explicit flag.
Risk: Divergent runtime environments (browsers vs servers) may behave differently under defaults. Mitigation: conservative browser defaults + clear docs and opt-in for aggressive strategies.
Risk: Existing customers depend on current retry behavior. Mitigation: release behind feature flag and provide migration playbook + automation to mirror old behavior if requested.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Connor Liu: Spike completed for Python + TS classifiers. Observed that 429 with small Retry-After headers (<=2s) should be retried aggressively; updated proposal to treat Retry-After < 1s as soft jitter dampener.
2025-02-18 - María Gomez (PM): Please ensure docs include 'How to disable SDK idempotency' for enterprise users with server-side dedupe. Also ask security to review header generation logic.
2025-02-25 - Design review (Alex Chen): UX for opt-in idempotency in JS should be a single boolean on the options bag, not a separate API. Agree to change builder surface.
2025-03-01 - SRE (Jordan Blake): Logging suggestion: include attempt number and classifier in logs and sample payload (no user PII). We'll add a structured log key redwood.retry.{attempt,class}.
2025-03-04 - Connor Liu: Implemented Go sentinel errors and added integration tests. Pushing RFC PR for common classifier into a shared repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-common/pull/198
